title: Fidelity delta anchoring and repair playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a cross-cutting process for detecting, anchoring, triaging, and repairing small-to-medium fidelity deltas that appear after model promotions, quantization, runtime changes (KV cache, batching), or prompt modifications. It is intended for Applied ML, Serving, and SRE teams collaborating to keep production quality within tolerance while preserving cost/latency improvements.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: production inference endpoints (hosted + dedicated), shadow environments used during canaries, and evaluation harness runs that mirror production workloads.
- Intent: provide a deterministic, low-friction workflow to localize cause (model, quant profile, runtime, prompts, or data drift) and apply the least-disruptive mitigation (fix prompt, routing, roll-forward of model variant, or targeted rollback).

Key definitions:
- Fidelity delta: measurable degradation in user-facing correctness or downstream QA metrics relative to the active baseline (can be absolute or relative change).
- Anchor probe set: curated small set of probes (<= 250 examples) that are stable, representative of critical slices, and annotated to detect subtle regressions.
- Golden baseline: the last certified model+config that satisfied the acceptance matrix for a given deployment.

Signals and telemetry (what to watch):
1) Primary signals (auto-alert):
   - Slice-level quality drop: > 4% relative drop in accuracy/intent-match on critical slices over a 6-hour window.
   - Semantic regression index (SRI): increase > 0.05 absolute on weighted slices.
   - Response drift score: embedding-distance drift > 0.12 from baseline cluster centroids.
2) Secondary signals (supporting evidence):
   - Token-level perplexity shift on prompt families.
   - Confusion in reranking/QA reranks (top-1 swap rate > 8%).
   - Latency/throughput correlated anomalies (may indicate batching/cache changes).

Anchoring strategy (how we establish a ground truth quickly):
1) Golden anchor run: rerun the anchor probe set on the current golden baseline artifact (model+quant profile+runtime flags). Capture full tokens, embeddings, and functioncall traces where applicable.
2) Delta anchor run: run the same probe set on the suspect artifact (promoted model or new quant profile or runtime change).
3) Comparison matrix: produce a compact delta report with the following rows (ASCII table example below):\n| slice | metric_baseline | metric_candidate | delta_abs | delta_rel | primary_failure_mode | notes |
|------|-----------------|------------------|----------:|---------:|---------------------|-------|
| invoice-parsing | 0.93 | 0.87 | -0.06 | -6.5% | hallucination | candidate undercounts totals |

(automated tooling will populate the full matrix; the ASCII example is for reviewers).

Triage playbook (step-by-step):
1) Alert receipt and first responder (15 min):
   - On-call eval engineer verifies alert and grabs the current golden and candidate artifacts IDs.
   - Run the anchor probe set if not already produced (use fast-path sampling to limit cost).
2) Fast isolation (30–60 min):
   - A/B narrow: split a 500-sample random subset of the failing slice and run with three configurations: golden, candidate, and candidate with quantization disabled (float fallback).
   - If candidate vs float-fallback shows no delta, mark quantization as primary suspect.
   - If candidate vs golden differ but candidate+no-cache equals golden, mark KV cache / prefix handling as suspect.
3) Root-cause experiments (1–4 hours):
   - Re-run with functioncall tracing and top-k tokens saved.
   - Run with temperature fixed at production value, and with alternative tokenizers (if tokenization drift suspected).
   - If sample-level differences are subtle, escalate to human annotators to label 50 examples for qualitative failure modes.
4) Decision matrix and mitigation (1–8 hours):
   - If quantization suspected and delta > threshold: immediately route 80% traffic to golden and 20% to candidate (preserve canary) and open a quant patch ticket.
   - If prompt drift: apply targeted prompt rewrite via prompt-layer hotfix and observe.
   - If model-level behavioral regression: rollback candidate or promote a hotfix variant that disables the risky head (see model rollback steps).

Runbook commands and tools (examples):
- Anchor probe run (eval-harness CLI):
  rdx-eval run --suite anchor-probes --baseline-id <golden-id> --out artifacts/golden-anchor.json --limit 250
  rdx-eval run --suite anchor-probes --candidate-id <candidate-id> --out artifacts/candidate-anchor.json --limit 250
- Quick diff summary (Python util):
  python tools/delta_summary.py --base artifacts/golden-anchor.json --cand artifacts/candidate-anchor.json --slices invoice-parsing,qa
- Quant fallback run:
  rdx-runtime request --model <candidate-id> --quant none --payload test-batch.json --out artifacts/cand-nofq.json

Example decision checklist (checkboxes for on-call):
1) Anchor probe runs completed: [ ]
2) Quant fallback tested: [ ]
3) KV cache disabled test: [ ]
4) Human annotation sample collected: [ ]
5) Mitigation route chosen (rollback/reroute/prompt-fix): [ ]
6) Post-mitigation validation run completed: [ ]

Mitigation patterns (preserve uptime while repairing):
- Traffic routing: use weighted routing (default to golden) with automatic decay to avoid flip-flopping.
- Prompt-layer hotfix: push minimal prompt correction that has been validated on anchor probes and a 1k-sample shadow run before unthrottled rollout.
- Quant profile patch: if quant introduced regression, produce a candidate quant profile that increases activation precision for the failing layer(s) and re-run micro-canary.
- Degraded-mode fallbacks: switch to a higher-latency but higher-fidelity model family for critical customers via tiered routing.

Model onboarding checklist (what must be present to make future regressions easier to diagnose):
- Artifact manifests: model id, architecture, tokenizer version, quant profile id, KV cache flags, runtime kernels used.
- Anchor probe run results: baseline and candidate reference artifacts stored with tags.
- Per-slice acceptance thresholds captured in metadata.
- Synthetic stress probes for KV-cache boundary conditions.
- Shadow-run telemetry: request traces, token-level logs (PII redacted), and response embeddings.

Quality guardrails to enable automatically (config examples):
- Auto-alert rule (example):
  name: slice-drop-critical
  condition: slice=\"billing-extract\" and delta_accuracy_rel <= -0.05 and window=\"6h\"
  action: page->eval-oncall, create_ticket->regression-triage
- Auto-fail gate for promotion: any candidate with SRI >= 0.06 on critical slices fails promotion.

Quantization-specific guidance:
- Always run a float (no-quant) micro-canary for the anchor probes before full promotion.
- Maintain a small library of per-architecture recovery quant profiles that trade latency for fidelity for prioritized slices.
- Track layer-level bitwidth changes and sample-level activation histograms for rapid comparison.

Documentation and artifacts to attach to every incident ticket:
- anchor_probe_{timestamp}_golden.json
- anchor_probe_{timestamp}_candidate.json
- delta_summary.html (automated diff report)
- sampled_token_traces.jsonl (max 1000 items)
- human_annotation_table.csv (if collected)

Escalation routing and ownership:
- Level 1 (on-call eval engineer): verify signals, run anchors, do fast isolation.
- Level 2 (model owner / quant expert): perform quant experiments, propose quant profile or model patch.
- Level 3 (serving-runtime / infra lead): investigate KV cache, batching, and kernel changes.
- Product/CS notification: if customer-impacting, notify account owners and CS for QBR-level customers.

Post-incident activities (within 3 days):
1) Annotate a canonical failure example and add to the probe-catalog with tags.
2) Synthesize a compact improvement ticket: either patch quant profile, add a prompt test, or update acceptance thresholds.
3) Run a 3-day shadow schedule to verify no recurrence.
4) If root cause was model training change, add a mandatory regeneration of a 1k-anchor probe set for the next promotion.

Appendix A — Minimal evaluation matrix (text table):
- Columns: test_family | probe_count | acceptance_threshold | runtime_flags_to_capture
- Rows:
  - anchor-stable: 200 | 0.94 accuracy | quant/kv-cache/seed
  - stress-kv-boundary: 100 | 0.98 pass-rate | prefix_len=4096, cache_enabled=true
  - prompt-perturbations: 150 | SRI <= 0.03 | tokenizer_version

Appendix B — Example short incident timeline (template to paste into ticket):
- 10:14 Alert triggered: billing-extract slice drop (-6.3%)
- 10:22 Anchor probes executed (golden + candidate)
- 11:05 Quant fallback run: delta disappears -> quant suspected
- 12:00 Route 80/20 golden/candidate while quant patch created
- 16:30 Quant patch promoted to canary, post-checks green
- 17:00 Repair ticket created and assigned to quant team (Q-1234)

Appendix C — Links and references:
- Eval harness docs: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/ (see runner and CLI docs)
- Quant profiles index: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/
- Regression triage playbooks: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/

Ownership and maintenance:
- Owner: Applied ML (probe & eval stewardship) + Serving runtime (runtime flags)
- Review cadence: quarterly review of anchor probe sets and thresholds, immediate retagging when model families change.

Contact (primary): Maya Chen (Applied ML) — maya@redwood.example.com

End of document.
